Enstar is warning about rolling blackouts and fielding new data center interest in the same week.
Alaska's one federal AI award points at the grid, not at the new load.

278 projects on the Department of Energy's Genesis Mission list, posted July 22.

Exactly one row is Alaska's, a UAF project called AURORA-AI, Alaska Utility Resilience and Optimization using Real-time AI.

Six days later Enstar president John Sims said a winter like last year's would likely bring rolling blackouts.

Inside, the award row as published, what two utility chiefs said, and the blanks in both.

The Anchorage Daily News reported Enstar is weighing new connections, citing data center interest.

No dollar figure has been published. No description either.

So what would Alaska's one row have to be worth, in dollars, before it counts as a federal answer to this winter?

#AlaskaEnergy #GenesisMission #Railbelt

Editor's note

Ships at 8.09 against a relaxed 7.7 threshold with zero hard fails, and it ships on its writing and its structure rather than on its pictures. Artwork craft is 6.0, the weakest criterion, for the ninth time in eleven runs. Half the diagnosis worked: the flat single-value-group failure that produced three straight 6.90s is measurably dead, and the cause turned out to be a loop direction rather than art direction, so the cover now falls from L 0.475 at the lit crest to L 0.120 at the near edge. The other half did not: the promised distributed detail never arrived, so the same contour drift and the same knockout plates repeat across six slides. TWO PROCESS SHORTFALLS, disclosed rather than buried. The copywriter room was not spawned, so the caption is the caption room's winner but the copy polish step did not run. And the deck-summary line that brand.yaml requires has now lapsed for a third consecutive run, which is a rule nobody enforces rather than an oversight; it needs either the room writing it or the config amended. Nothing here blocks posting.

AKSNOW.surface() draws a modelled snow mass from a crest contour with (1) a ridge drawn as a LIT windward edge plus a DARK lee edge rather than a single stroke, (2) line weight that tapers along each mark and scales with depth instead of two fixed widths, (3) specular crest glints, (4) a wind-polish micro-streak population filling the space between ridges, and (5) an order-independent value ladder drawn as strips.
